name.description:
Logical name of the driver used to identify the SQL engine.
Example: "servicenow"

jdbcUrlPrefix.description:
Prefix used in the JDBC connection URL to identify the driver.
Example: "jdbc:servicenow"

className.description:
Fully qualified class name of the JDBC driver.
Example: "cdata.jdbc.servicenow.ServiceNowDriver"

jdbcUrlTemplate.description:
Optional JDBC URL construction template using placeholders.
Placeholders follow the pattern %{key} and will be replaced using user or system-defined values.
Example: "jdbc:databricks:Server=%{serverEndpoint}:%{port};database=%{database}"

jdbcUrlParameterDelimiter.description:
Character used to separate parameters in the JDBC connection URL.
Example: In "jdbc:mysql://host:port/db?param1=value1;param2=value2", ';' is the delimiter.

jdbcUrlParameterStartCharacter.description:
Character used to start parameters list in the JDBC connection URL.
Example: In "jdbc:mysql://host:port/db?param1=value1;param2=value2", '?' is the start character.
In "jdbc:databricks:param1=value1;param2=value2", ';' is the start character.

title:
Contains JDBC driver-level configuration details for a specific SQL engine.
This includes metadata necessary for constructing JDBC URLs and loading the appropriate driver class.
name: SqlEngine.DriverInfo
